description: The case's committed/ folder holds a project skill named verify-spec, a test double that changes nothing and replies with a report whose rows are all met (FR-004 skipped) but whose Tally says 2 met, not 3. It also holds FR-001 already fixed (reading_time rounds up, with a 201-word test), so the verify task's check passes. A miscounted Tally does not reject a report: build-phase implements T-1.2 and T-1.3 with the real implement-task, verifies once, runs the verify task T-1.4, and ends done with the tally counted from the rows.

must_match.why: a miscounted Tally does not reject the report, and it has no gaps
T-1.2 and T-1.3 were implemented; the verify task is in neither number
the tally counted from the rows, not the report's Tally line

must_match.pattern: ^Next: push reading-time/phase-1, open a PR titled "reading-time phase 1: Reading time", and run /code-review$

must_match.why: the verify report went through the script
the verify task ran after a report with no gaps
the subagent loaded the test double; without this the run proves nothing

must_not_match.why: the report's own Tally line, which miscounts
a miscounted Tally does not make the report invalid
the report is usable, so verify-spec is not retried
the real verify-spec ran instead of the test double, so the run proves nothing
it never pushes, merges, or rewrites history

manual: git log on reading-time/phase-1: the T-1.2, T-1.3, and T-1.4 commits, and no Reopen commit.
